extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to perform web traversal by systematically traversing a website's subpages to extract high-quality data. It uses a Question-Answer format to assess traversal and problem-solving capabilities in web scenarios across education, conference, organization, and game domains.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. First stage: GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and pages, constructing queries, and filtering for legitimate QA pairs. Second stage: crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) with accessible sub-links and their respective pages. The raw data consists of web page markdown content and clickable HTML buttons extracted using Beautiful Soup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-stage funnel annotation strategy: Stage 1 - GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing websites, constructing queries, and filtering for legitimate QA pairs with short answers containing entities. Stage 2 - Crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human annotators verify and ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent through manual verification to ensure accuracy and relevance
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o used for initial annotations including traversing websites, constructing queries based on page information and specified roles, and filtering for legitimate queries with short answers containing entities
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. The dataset only utilizes HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons and does not incorporate multimodal environments such as visual modalities (screenshots). The dataset is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, while pre-trained models rely on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date and lack dynamic updates.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions. It can be used for training (with approximately 14k silver QA pairs as supplementary training data), testing, and validation of web navigation and information-seeking capabilities. The dataset supports agent tuning through fine-tuning models with golden trajectories.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The WebWalkerQA dataset will be available at HuggingFace Datasets. Code for WebWalker will be released on GitHub.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset includes both multi-source and single-source types, corresponding to two types of human information-seeking behaviours. Questions are categorized into three difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard) based on page depth. Multi-source QA tasks are designed to prevent exploitation by search engine shortcuts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. Stage 1: GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing websites, constructing queries, and filtering for legitimate queries with short entity-based answers. Stage 2: Human annotators conduct quality control, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency.

Multimodal Environment: In this work, we only utilize HTML-DOM to parse clickable buttons... WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, while pre-trained models rely on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date and lack dynamic updates.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: WebWalkerQA, designed specifically to evaluate LLMs on their ability to handle queries embedded in complex, multi-step web interactions on a given root website... Additionally, we possess a collection of approximately 14k silver QA pairs, which, although not yet carefully human-verified, can serve as supplementary training data to enhance agent performance... Agent Tuning: WebWalker is driven by prompting without additional training. We can use agent tuning to help LLMs learn web traversal. This involves fine-tuning models with golden trajectories, enabling them to take effective actions for completing information-seeking tasks.
